main_text.l: Numerant Copti per literas ut reliqui Ori-
entales, & hos numeros ut & literarum fere
omnium nomina & figuras à Graecis Ptolo-
maeorum tempore mutati sunt, addunt virgu-
lam supra literam ut Arabes; in millenariis
vero infra, habent & alias numerorum notas
sibi proprias.
SECT. II.
Vida, seu v consona, effertur ut b.
Hida, similis est Graecae literae (η) & sonat
ut I declinans ad E, at cum habet accentum
sonat ut I clarum.
Ni in fine dictionis formam mutat, & ex-
tenditur infra lineam, ut Hebraicum mun in
fine ן[?].
Thida ut Θ effertur.
Bi, ut P.
Dau, ut D:
He, aliquando ut I, & (y) & post Alpha ut
(v) vocalis.
Phi, aliquando P. declinans ad B.
Chi, absque aspiratione ut χ Graecum à
Gallis.
Ebsi, ut [illegible, ~1 letter].
Scei, ut Sc. ut ש[?] Hebræum & ش Arab-cum.

page.notes: The Greek eta, theta and chi are read from the printed forms; "(y)" is printed in Latin letters as shown. The Hebrew final letter after "mun in fine" (printed as a hooked stroke below the line) is uncertain: read as ן[?]. The glyph after "Ebsi, ut" is unclear and marked illegible. The Hebrew letter after "Sc. ut" is uncertain (ש[?]). The Arabic letter after "&" is read as ش from a small, unclear printed form. The large initial V of "Vida" is joined to the word as printed. Bottom right: the catchword "Chei," is printed, and the page number is "(110)" in old numerals.
